solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Carefully study stanza and discuss (8)

blocks.note: to con is to pore over, as in conning a script
a verse is a stanza of a poem

annotation.surface: A poetry seminar: read the stanza closely, then talk it over.
annotation.walkthrough: CON is an old verb for studying closely, still met in crosswords far more than in speech.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: conversing is talking things over.

entries.clue: With eight members the Spanish set firm up (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
to set something down is to put it
Co = company, a firm

annotation.surface: A Spanish octet sets up a company together.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole run EL+PUT+CO is built first, then turned upside down to read OCTUPLE.
annotation.definitionFit: Octuple means eightfold, made up of eight parts or members.

entries.clue: Victor somehow done with right and left — see new politician (3,3,5)

indicators.note: done 'somehow' is done rearranged in some way or other

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
DONE rearranged
R = right
L = left
to eye something is to see it
N = new

annotation.surface: A victor's work done, with right and left looking on at a newcomer to politics.
annotation.walkthrough: Ursula von der Leyen is the German politician who became President of the European Commission.
annotation.definitionFit: Von der Leyen is a politician, a European Commission president.

entries.clue: Wake from sleep — plan to introduce oxygen (5)

indicators.note: the plan takes in, or introduces, the oxygen

blocks.note: a ruse is a scheme or plan
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

annotation.surface: A scheme to get someone up by pumping oxygen into the room.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits definition from wordplay; 'plan' is a noun here, a scheme, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb, as in rousing someone at dawn.

entries.clue: No inclination to listen to school board (7)

indicators.note: listen with no LIST keeps only what is left

blocks.note: LISTEN without LIST, a list being a lean or inclination
to school a horse or pupil is to train it

annotation.surface: A pupil with no wish to pay attention to the school board.
annotation.walkthrough: The trick is reading 'inclination' as LIST, a ship's lean, and removing it from 'listen'. 'School board' looks like one noun but splits into verb and definition.
annotation.definitionFit: To entrain is to board a train, a rare but real word.

entries.clue: Plate hot starter in Raffles: happen to devour that? (6)

indicators.note: the starter of a word is its first letter
happen swallows, or devours, the letters

blocks.note: to come about is to happen
H = hot, on taps
first letter of Raffles

annotation.surface: A diner at Raffles hotel in Singapore wonders whether to eat a hot starter off the plate.
annotation.walkthrough: Raffles is the famous Singapore hotel, which makes 'Plate' look like dinnerware; it means chromium plating here.
annotation.definitionFit: Chrome is chromium plate, as on a car's trim.

entries.clue: Drink packed with fruit, and cheers for the sausage (9)

indicators.note: the drink is packed, or filled, with the fruit

blocks.note: a cola is a soft drink
a hip is the fruit of the rose
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

annotation.surface: A fruity drink and a thank-you offered to someone serving sausages.
annotation.walkthrough: A hip is the red fruit of the wild rose, a sense easy to miss when 'fruit' suggests apples. A chipolata is a small thin British sausage.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: the chipolata is a small, thin British variety.

entries.clue: Aggressive behaviour Proust periodically exhibited (3)

indicators.note: shown at regular intervals, every other letter

blocks.note: the even letters of pRoUsT

annotation.surface: A literary critic spots flashes of aggression in Proust's novels.
annotation.walkthrough: The rut is the season when male deer turn aggressive and fight.
annotation.definitionFit: A hunting term: the rutting season is when stags fight over mates.

entries.clue: Instrument doctor’s used to probe a von Trapp (7)

indicators.note: the doctor goes into the von Trapp like a probe

blocks.note: Maria von Trapp, heroine of The Sound of Music
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor

annotation.surface: A doctor examines one of the singing von Trapp family.
annotation.walkthrough: Maria is the governess who marries into the von Trapp family in The Sound of Music; the 's reads as 'doctor is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A marimba is a musical instrument, a large wooden xylophone.

entries.clue: See t-tutoring tricky to take in with tortuous talking test? (6-7)

indicators.note: the letters are handled in a tricky, twisted way
the anagram fodder takes in the W as well

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
W = with

annotation.surface: A stammering tutor tries to teach a tongue-twister, and the clue itself stumbles over its T-sounds.
annotation.walkthrough: The stutter in 't-tutoring' supplies the extra T the anagram needs, so it is fodder, not decoration.
annotation.definitionFit: A tongue-twister is a phrase that tests your ability to speak it through its twists.

entries.clue: Parched, stopped by pub: The Globe (6)

indicators.note: the pub plugs, or stops, the middle of the word

blocks.note: sere is a poetic word for dried up
PH, public house, on British maps

annotation.surface: A thirsty drinker stops at a pub called The Globe.
annotation.walkthrough: The Globe looks like the name of a pub, which suits the surface; it is really just a globe, a sphere.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: any globe is a ball shape, and 'The' just reads along with it.

entries.clue: Article horde rotated in vault is WMD (4,4)

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters read backwards
the turned horde goes inside the vault

blocks.note: a is the indefinite article
a burial vault is a tomb
MOB, a horde, turned round

annotation.surface: A news item: a mob has hidden a weapon of mass destruction in a vault.
annotation.walkthrough: WMD, weapons of mass destruction, is the definition, and 'is' links it to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: An atom bomb is a weapon of mass destruction.

entries.clue: Outlaw hit and killed by fragments (5,3,3)

indicators.note: the words are broken into fragments and reassembled

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters, skipping the joining 'and'

annotation.surface: An outlaw shot and killed by shrapnel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fragments' reads as a noun, the thing that killed him, but works as a verb telling you to break the letters up.
annotation.definitionFit: Billy the Kid was a notorious outlaw of the American Wild West.

entries.clue: Trouble coming after ring names a drug supplier (10)

blocks.note: to ring someone is to give them a bell
ado is fuss or trouble
N = name, doubled for the plural
a as itself

annotation.surface: After a phone call, trouble: someone names a drug dealer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drug supplier' suggests a dealer, but it is the plant: deadly nightshade yields the drugs atropine and belladonna.
annotation.definitionFit: Belladonna, deadly nightshade, is a plant that supplies drugs.

entries.clue: Henry feeding daughter diet that’s immortal? (9)

indicators.note: Henry is fed into the middle of the diet

blocks.note: D = daughter
to diet is to eat less
H, the henry, is the unit of inductance

annotation.surface: Henry puts his daughter on a diet, hoping it will make her live for ever.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Diet' is a verb phrase here, what you do to slim, and Henry is the unit of inductance rather than a king.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, the poetic sense of fame or verse that never dies.

entries.clue: Get the round in — that which may be carried (4)

blocks.note: the round is a bullet or shell, put into the breech of a gun
a burden or cargo, what a porter or lorry carries

annotation.surface: Buying drinks at the pub, and carrying them back to the table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get the round in' is British pub talk for buying drinks for your group; here the round is ammunition and you load the gun.
annotation.definitionFit: Loading puts a round in the gun; a load is what gets carried.

entries.clue: Comply with old Turkish governor (4)

blocks.note: O = old
a bey was an Ottoman provincial governor

annotation.surface: Doing what an old Ottoman governor says.
annotation.walkthrough: BEY is a crossword regular from the Ottoman Empire, alongside DEY and AGA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for following an order or rule.

entries.clue: French cheese stores have rich cake (7)

indicators.note: the cheese stores, or holds, the other word

blocks.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
to have something is to own it

annotation.surface: A shop's cheese counter sits next to the chocolate cakes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stores' reads as shops in the surface but works as a verb, holding something inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by kind: the brownie is a dense chocolate traybake.

entries.clue: Dance where the last shall be first in mock revelation (10)

indicators.text: where the last shall be first
indicators.note: the final letter moves to the front, echoing the Gospel saying
the altered dance sits inside the mock

blocks.note: to ape is to mimic or mock

blocks.clueFragment: Dance where the last shall be first
blocks.note: CALYPSO with its last letter O moved to the front

annotation.surface: A Gospel line quoted at a dance that mocks the end of the world.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The last shall be first' comes from the Bible, fitting the biblical answer. Apocalypse means revelation, the Greek name of the Book of Revelation.
annotation.definitionFit: Apocalypse is Greek for revelation, the name of the Bible's last book.

entries.clue: Group from the south races alien in green (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, read from the bottom up, so backwards
the races and alien sit inside green

blocks.note: eco = environmentally green
the TT races on the Isle of Man
ET, the film's extraterrestrial

annotation.surface: A band from the south of the galaxy races an alien in a green car.
annotation.walkthrough: TTET goes inside ECO to make ETTETCO, which read upwards gives OCTETTE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for a band of eight, in the older French-style spelling.

entries.clue: Having circled both poles, track back (7)

indicators.note: the track goes round the poles

blocks.note: spoor is an animal's track
N and S, the north and south poles

annotation.surface: A polar explorer, having gone round both poles, retraces the route home.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Track back' looks like one instruction to retrace, but back is the definition, a verb meaning support.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the funding sense, backing a charity walker or a team.

entries.clue: Cheeky display preceding second-hand books launch? (8)

blocks.note: mooning is baring one's cheeks, the buttocks
s/h, short for second-hand in ads
OT, the Old Testament books

annotation.surface: A cheeky stunt promotes the launch of a second-hand bookshop.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a moonshot as an example of a launch, a rocket to the moon.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, hence the question mark: the moon landings began as literal launches.

entries.clue: Quiet party ushered inside notice seaport (6)

indicators.note: the quiet party is shown in, placed inside the notice

blocks.note: an ad is a notice
sh! calls for quiet
a do is a party

annotation.surface: A discreet party guest is shown in past a notice at the harbour.
annotation.walkthrough: Ashdod is Israel's largest port, on the Mediterranean.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one particular port, on Israel's Mediterranean coast.

entries.clue: Enlightened sort, a bowler perhaps restricting runs (5)

indicators.note: to restrict is to hem something in, so the hat closes around the runs and holds them

blocks.note: a as itself
a bowler is a kind of hat
R = runs, in cricket scoring

annotation.surface: A wise cricket bowler keeps the batsmen from scoring runs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bowler' and 'runs' both paint cricket, but the bowler is a hat. An arhat is a Buddhist who has reached enlightenment.
annotation.definitionFit: An arhat is a Buddhist saint who has attained enlightenment.

entries.clue: Harry Kane rages — shot unexceptional (2,5,6)

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, pushing the letters about

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: The England striker Harry Kane fumes after an ordinary shot.
annotation.walkthrough: Harry Kane is England's football captain, so 'Harry' reads as his first name, not a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: No great shakes means not very good, unexceptional.

entries.clue: Leaders of Greeks, Italians, and Norwegians in Geneva (3)

indicators.note: the leading, first letters of each word

blocks.clueFragment: Leaders of Greeks, Italians, and Norwegians
blocks.note: first letters of Greeks, Italians, Norwegians

annotation.surface: European leaders gathered for a summit in Geneva.
annotation.walkthrough: Geneva is an old name for gin, from the Dutch jenever, not the Swiss city.
annotation.definitionFit: Geneva is an old word for gin, via Dutch jenever.

entries.clue: Group round bar back for court proceedings (6)

indicators.note: the group goes round the bar
the result reads backwards

blocks.note: a set is a group
an inn is a bar or pub

annotation.surface: A group gathers round a bar after legal proceedings.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Court proceedings' sounds like law, but it means what happens on a tennis court. The container is built first and the whole thing then read backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on court: the proceedings are games played on a court, not a hearing.

entries.clue: External layer red with comet disintegrating (8)

indicators.note: the comet breaks up, and so do its letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A red comet breaking up, its outer layer burning off.
annotation.walkthrough: The ectoderm is the outermost layer of cells in an embryo.
annotation.definitionFit: A biology term: the outermost of an embryo's three germ layers.
